answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with audited work bonds. A newcomer starts with only an ember of trust: it locks a small bond and must complete real, verifiable jobs assigned at random, whose outputs peers spot-check. Each verified job adds a layer to its pearl of reputation, and the bond is released only gradually as that record thickens. One identity can graze the shared meadow only after proving itself, so an attacker creating thousands of fakes must pay a bond, pass real work, and survive audits for every one — the cost grows with each fake, while honest agents pay it just once.
